gaps: The MOE entry establishes that a current authoritative dictionary recognizes plural uses of bare 你, but its examples are cited from historical works. This pass did not establish the frequency or register of bare-你 plural use in present-day speech; the usual modern 你们 form should remain separately described.
The local 字源 entries for 尔 and 爾 and the CUHK 爾 account describe distinct graphic-origin analyses. Their claims are attributed findings and do not resolve the formation of 你 itself.

No inspected source directly demonstrates whether 你 was formed phonosemantically from 亻 plus 尔 or ideographically from 人 plus 尔. The right-side form and proposed sound role should remain separated; the sound role is unresolved by the sources inspected here.
